title: Game Developers Launch Itch.io Bundle to Fund Relief for Laid-Off Workers
excerpt: The Game Industry Hardship Fund bundle, organized by Necrosoft Games and the United Videogame Workers union, offers over 100 DRM-free games for $10 with all proceeds supporting laid-off developers in the US and Canada.
body:
• Over 100 indie games available for a minimum $10 on itch.io, with all proceeds funding cash grants of up to $5,000 for laid-off game developers in the US and Canada.
  • The bundle, organized by Necrosoft Games and the United Videogame Workers-CWA union, raised over $20,000 within its first day and runs through August 13.
  • Roughly one-third of US game developers have been laid off in the past two years, according to the 2026 GDC State of the Game Industry report.

A coalition of more than 100 indie game developers has banded together to sell a charity bundle on digital storefront itch.io, directing all proceeds toward a hardship fund for colleagues laid off during the video game industry's prolonged downturn.

The Game Industry Hardship Fund bundle, which launched on July 30, is organized by Brandon Sheffield of Demonschool developer Necrosoft Games in partnership with the United Videogame Workers-CWA (UVW-CWA), a union affiliated with the Communications Workers of America. The pay-what-you-want bundle carries a minimum price of $10 and had already crossed $20,000 in sales within a day of going live, according to Kotaku.

A Safety Net Built by Peers

The bundle offers DRM-free PC versions of titles including the acclaimed exploration game A Short Hike, skateboarding adventure SkateBIRD, and puzzle game Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure. All revenue, minus itch.io's processing fees, flows directly to the UVW-CWA's Game Worker Hardship Fund.

Eligible applicants — developers, contractors, or freelancers laid off after January 2024 — can request either a small grant of up to $1,000 or a larger sum between $1,000 and $5,000. The money can cover basic living expenses such as groceries, rent, and medical bills. Applicants do not need to be union members.

"Too many people are out of work and the jobs they could fill are disappearing as CEOs try to replace them with AI."

— Necrosoft Games, bundle description

The UVW-CWA, which is local 9433 of the Communications Workers of America and a 501(c)(5) organization, will handle all fund distribution independently. Sheffield and Necrosoft's role is limited to organizing the bundle; they have no involvement in dispersing the money.

An Industry in Crisis

The bundle arrives against a grim backdrop. According to the 2026 GDC State of the Game Industry report, more than a quarter of game developers globally have been laid off in the past two years. In the United States alone, that figure rises to roughly one-third.

The layoffs have swept through studios of every size. Large publishers and small independents alike have cut staff, often despite releasing critically and commercially successful titles. The wave has left thousands of skilled professionals scrambling for work in an industry that appears to be contracting even as revenues grow.

Sheffield is no stranger to organizing large-scale itch.io charity bundles. Necrosoft Games previously spearheaded the Bundle for Ukraine, which raised over $6.3 million, and the California Fire Relief Bundle. Both efforts demonstrated the indie game community's capacity to mobilize quickly around causes that matter to its members.

Community Solidarity in a Contracting Market

The bundle's organizers imposed strict curation rules. All submitted games must be paid titles that have never been offered for free. No generative AI content of any kind is permitted. Tabletop RPGs are accepted in limited quantities, and explicit sexual content is excluded to maximize the bundle's reach.

For South Asian professionals in the gaming industry — a growing presence across studios in North America — the layoff wave has added visa-related complications to an already precarious situation. Workers on employer-sponsored visas face tight windows to find new positions or risk losing their immigration status, making funds like UVW-CWA's hardship grants particularly critical.

What's Next

The bundle will remain available for purchase through August 13, giving buyers a two-week window. Laid-off developers in the US and Canada can apply for hardship assistance through the UVW-CWA website, with a volunteer review team prioritizing applications based on urgency.

The union plans to publish an impact report toward the end of the year documenting how the funds were used. Whether this initiative can scale to match the magnitude of the crisis remains to be seen, but it represents one of the most direct peer-to-peer support mechanisms the industry has produced.
nri_angle: South Asian game industry professionals on employer-sponsored visas face heightened vulnerability during layoffs, making peer-driven hardship funds especially relevant.
